decision_reason: A1 already separates the vigorous unseen activities through intensity, cadence, impacts and locomotion. Its closest unseen pair, sitting versus standing, lacks a defensible additional distinction with an unconstrained user-carried phone and wrist watch; global posture remains placement-dependent. The clearest conservative refinement is to distinguish local wrist reorientation from global posture variability. This adds a transferable contrast for eating soup versus writing, whose A1 prototypes differ only in intensity, using seen feeding and manipulation activities as anchors. It may also help characterize brushing teeth, but does not assume a particular brushing technique. No reliable extra distinction is asserted for eating soup versus eating sandwich, or for sitting versus standing.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_orientation_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of change in the wrist-worn watch's gravity-relative orientation within a window, independent of global body posture and repetition rate.

levels.Low: Wrist orientation remains within a narrow gravity-relative range.
levels.Medium: Wrist orientation spans a moderate gravity-relative range.
levels.High: Wrist orientation spans a broad gravity-relative range.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable acceleration and angular-motion magnitude. Retaining this broad contrast transfers from walking, stairs and ball activities to jogging and kicking (soccer ball), both relatively weakly covered in A1. Effort, phone carriage and whether the watch-bearing arm participates can blur levels; magnitude alone does not identify the active limb.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in accelerometer and gyroscope motion. It transfers gait-rate structure from walking to jogging and rapid manual repetition from typing to brushing teeth. Pauses, short windows and multiple periodic units can make rate ambiguous; rate is not equated with regularity.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid signal change rather than isolated peaks. This retains the existing eating soup versus eating sandwich contrast and transfers continuous-motion semantics from writing and drinking from cup. Movement speed and transmitted vibration can affect apparent smoothness, so a smooth utensil trajectory is not assumed for every execution.

impulsiveness: G10 supports short abrupt acceleration or rotation changes, preserving impact-related transfer from clapping and ball activities to jogging and kicking (soccer ball). Foot or ball contact may be attenuated at the phone and wrist, and incidental handling can create peaks; this is not a direct contact detector.

posture_inclination: G1 provides gravity-relative orientation evidence when a carried device has a sufficiently stable relation to the body. Preserve the existing concept rather than invent another sitting versus standing cue. Transfer from writing and walking is conditional: phone orientation and wrist pose are not global body inclination, and an upright seated trunk may resemble standing. The supplied sitting-versus-standing distinction is therefore weakly observable, not guaranteed.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative orientation when device motion reflects the load-bearing body. Retention preserves transfer from stairs and playing catch w/tennis ball to jogging and kicking (soccer ball). Loose phone carriage and isolated arm movement can mimic body-posture changes; wrist orientation variation must not be treated as sufficient evidence of global variation.

rotational_motion: G2 supports sustained angular motion observable by the gyroscopes. This retains transfer from eating pasta and drinking from cup to brushing teeth, and from playing catch w/tennis ball to kicking (soccer ball). Technique and watch-side participation affect evidence; prominent rotation does not necessarily imply a broad gravity-relative orientation range.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies, retaining locomotor transfer from walking and stairs to jogging and the existing kicking (soccer ball) versus playing catch w/tennis ball contrast. Local arm translation and proxy drift can resemble progression; the available evidence does not establish absolute speed or distance.

motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and temporal predictability independently of repetition rate. Walking and dribbling (basketball) provide structured-motion anchors for jogging and brushing teeth, while irregular ball exchanges anchor kicking (soccer ball). Pauses, window duration and nearly static signals can complicate interpretation; high regularity need not imply active periodic motion.

wrist_orientation_variability: G12 supports the range of gravity-relative watch orientation, with G2 providing corroborating angular-motion evidence. Reorientation during hand-to-mouth transport offers an additional, physically plausible eating soup versus writing contrast beyond their single A1 intensity difference; drinking from cup, eating sandwich and eating pasta provide seen transport anchors, while writing and typing anchor constrained wrist orientation. This concerns orientation range, not movement speed, global posture or inferred utensil identity. Expected predictability is conditional: watch placement is known, but the active hand is not; a spoon may stay approximately level, writing can involve wrist rotation, and dynamic acceleration can obscure gravity. No fixed soup-versus-sandwich ordering or guaranteed brushing-teeth distinction is asserted.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes retain distinct physical meanings. Intensity describes magnitude; cadence describes repetition rate; regularity describes predictability. Smoothness concerns sustained rapid fluctuations, whereas impulsiveness concerns brief peaks. Mean global inclination and global posture variation differ from local wrist orientation range. Rotational prominence can be high during fast, small-range oscillations without broad wrist reorientation, so it is not equivalent to the added attribute. Translation denotes progression rather than local wrist transport. The addition is intentionally limited to one local orientation concept: no utensil identity, mouth proximity, leg-specific motion or seated joint configuration is inferred. Sitting versus standing and subtle feeding pairs remain unresolved where placement or execution prevents reliable IMU evidence.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
